Subject: PrivGPU capacity kickoff — baseline targets & topology ask

Hi Jordan / Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for agreeing to take a first pass at sizing our private GPU deployment. High-level targets from our side:
- Peak workload: ~2,000 requests per minute (RPM) with burst windows up to 3,500 RPM (5–10 minute bursts).
- Average request payload: ~256 tokens; p50 response size ~180 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms (end-to-end).
- Multi-tenant: 3 service teams sharing the pool; tenancy isolation preferred but we need cost efficiency.

Key asks for the initial runbook:
1) Bottleneck matrix (GPU compute, vCPU, NIC/egress pressure) mapping to target RPM ranges.
2) NAT/SNAT sizing and topology recommendations for VPC on our cloud (we run in 2 AZs per region).
3) Suggested autoscale curve and warm-pool strategy (warmup times, cache prefill).
4) Expected headroom for failover (minutes to recover to 100% capacity if one AZ degraded).

We have a quick internal doc with request patterns here: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-privgpu — happy to join a sync but would appreciate a written matrix first.

Paul

All —

Attached is the first-pass capacity matrix (privgpu_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a quick NAT sketch (nat_topology_sketch_v2.png). Summary of the sizing assumptions and recommendations below.

WORKLOAD ASSUMPTIONS (from Acme):
- Peak: 3,500 RPM (burst), steady peak 2,000 RPM.
- Avg tokens/request: 256.
- Desired p95 latency <= 350ms.

SERVER/INFRA ASSUMPTIONS:
- Model family: FP16-optimized 70B equivalent (latency profile similar to Llama-family large variant).
- Baseline GPU for sizing: A40 / 48GB (on-prem equivalent), conservative per-GPU throughput measured in our lab.
- Batching: continuous, with dynamic batching up to 8 requests/batch (batch size distribution heavily skewed small).

RECOMMENDATIONS (first pass):
1) Compute sizing (two-AZ active-active):
   - Steady peak (2,000 RPM => 33.3 req/s): with average 256 tokens/request, and expected per-request token-generation time, measured per-A40 GPU throughput ~8–10 req/s (no aggressive quantization).
   - Using batching and optimized kernel selection: effective throughput can be ~22–26 req/s per GPU during steady windows.
   - Recommendation: start with 6 GPUs (3 per AZ) to cover steady peaks with ~25–30% headroom. For bursts to 3,500 RPM, we recommend burst capacity to 10 GPUs (5 per AZ) via warm-pool + rapid scale (adds ~45–60s to reach target if cold).

2) Network / Egress sizing:
   - Average egress per request ~0.2KB (small), but KV/cache and model shard pulls during cold starts can spike egress per-GPU up to 1.2–1.8 Gbps.
   - Provision per-host NIC at 10Gbps; plan 2–3 GPUs per host when using 10Gbps NICs to avoid NIC saturation during cache misses.
   - NAT sizing: allocate SNAT ports with cushion — estimate 12k ephemeral mappings for peak concurrency across tenants. Per-AZ NAT gateway with 20k port capacity recommended for safer headroom.

3) Autoscale & warm-pool strategy:
   - Maintain a minimum warm-pool of 2 GPUs per AZ to reduce cold-start tail latency.
   - Scale-up policy: CPU/GPU utilization AND queued request depth triggers — e.g., scale when 1-minute average GPU utilization > 65% or request queue length > 8.
   - Scale-down: conservative decay with cool-down of 10 minutes to avoid oscillation.

4) Admission-control and graceful degradation:
   - Implement per-tenant concurrency quotas and request prioritization. For overload, fall back to a quantized model variant (lower-cost path) automatically.
   - Circuit-breaker: when p95 latency exceeds 600ms for >90s, shift new traffic to lower-Q model or alternate region.

5) Failure domains & headroom:
   - Active-active two AZs with even split provides automatic absorption if one AZ loses 40–50% capacity. With recommended headroom, recovery to target requires warming extra GPUs (45–90s depending on prefill).

TRADE-OFFS:
- More GPUs per host reduces NIC pressure but increases cost; we prefer 2–3 GPUs per 10Gb host for your profile.
- Strongly recommend 25–30% committed GPU buffer during business hours for predictable latency.

I'll convert this into the PDF summary (privgpu_capacity_report_v1.pdf) and share a one-pager for procurement.

Attachments: privgpu_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with calculations), nat_topology_sketch_v2.png (sketch)

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of detail we needed. A few clarifying Qs:
1) For the 6-GPU baseline (3/az), is that assuming 2–3 GPUs per host? If so we'll size hosts accordingly.
2) NAT gateway: our cloud has a per-AZ managed NAT with 16k SNAT port default — do you recommend we request a quota increase to 20k per-AZ?
3) Procurement ask: can you produce a short bill of materials (hosts, NICs, estimated monthly egress) for our procurement team?

If you can share the PDF and the spreadsheet we can circulate internally. Suggest we take the Monday sync — I'll propose times.

Paul

Subject: Re: PrivGPU capacity kickoff — baseline targets & topology ask

Paul —

Short answers inline:
1) Yes — the 6-GPU baseline assumes 2 GPUs per 10Gb host (3 hosts across two AZs), which balances NIC headroom and per-host costs. If you want stronger isolation, move to 1–2 GPUs per host and add hosts accordingly.
2) We recommend requesting NAT port quota to 20k per-AZ (16k default is tight for your peak concurrency and multi-tenant mapping). We'll include the quota justification in the BOM.
3) I'll attach the BOM (privgpu_capacity_report_v1.pdf) and the spreadsheet (privgpu_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx) in this thread. Procurement notes: include 25% reserved buffer for committed capacity + a one-time allowance for warm-pool (2 GPUs per AZ).

Next steps / action items:
- Jordan: attach PDF + spreadsheet (done).
- Marissa: draft operational runbook (drain/patch/warm-pool triggers) by Monday COB.
- Karthik: finalize microbench numbers for A40 vs A100 variants (timeline: Tue EOD).
- Paul: request NAT quota increase; confirm procurement timeline.

Thanks — happy to walk through in Monday's sync.
